page: Microsoft Azure E32_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev3 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server includes 819 GB of bundled local SSD storage and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is relatively low, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores in the middle 50%. Memory read bandwidth is average at 56.65 GB/sec for large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weaker, placing in the bottom 25%. Computational workloads like bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang achieve average throughput when multi-threaded, but single-threaded text processing and compression tasks are notably slower.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32_v3 offers a dense memory profile and bundled local SSD storage, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The instance is well-suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks. It is less optimal for single-threaded applications, high-performance computing, or large-scale LLM inference, where its older CPU architecture and lower single-core speeds present clear performance trade-offs.
